subproblems.title: Linear algebra of the co-area Jacobian: vanishing criterion and the chart identity (Lemma L)
subproblems.statement:
Let N, m, n, k ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝᴺ, f : ℝᴺ → ℝᵐ and x ∈ ℝᴺ. Put T := tangentSpace M x (a linear subspace of ℝᴺ with the induced inner product), D := fderiv ℝ f x and L := D|_T : T → ℝᵐ, so that coareaJacobian M f x = √det(L L*).
(1) If A : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ is a continuous linear map with T = range A, then coareaJacobian M f x = 0 if and only if D ∘ A : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ is not surjective.
(2) Let P := WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ) be the Euclidean product, with first component p₁ = WithLp.fst p. Suppose A : P → ℝᴺ is an injective continuous linear map with T = range A and D(A p) = p₁ for all p ∈ P. Suppose B : ℝᵏ → ℝᴺ is a continuous linear map with B b = A(toLp(0, b)) for all b ∈ ℝᵏ. Then coareaJacobian M f x · normDet(A) = normDet(B), where normDet is Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet, normDet(X) = √det(X*X).
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (N m n : ℕ) (M : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m) (x : Rn N) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn N), tangentSpace M x = LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap → (coareaJacobian M f x = 0 ↔ ¬ Function.Surjective ((fderiv ℝ f x).comp A))) ∧ ∀ (N m k : ℕ) (M : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m) (x : Rn N) (A : WithLp 2 (Rn m × Rn k) →L[ℝ] Rn N) (B : Rn k →L[ℝ] Rn N), Function.Injective A → tangentSpace M x = LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap → (∀ p, fderiv ℝ f x (A p) = WithLp.fst p) → (∀ b, B b = A (WithLp.toLp 2 (0, b))) → coareaJacobian M f x * A.toLinearMap.normDet = B.toLinearMap.normDet
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 0.2(a), 0.2(b) (Lemma L) and 3.3 of the parent proof, i.e. the linear algebra of Simon 6.2, specialized to the frozen definition coareaJacobian.

Notation.
- T := tangentSpace M x, a linear subspace of ℝᴺ carrying the restricted inner product.
- ι : T → ℝᴺ is the inclusion and D := fderiv ℝ f x : ℝᴺ → ℝᵐ.
- L := D ∘ ι : T → ℝᵐ; this is (fderiv ℝ f x).comp (tangentSpace M x).subtypeL. L* : ℝᵐ → T is its adjoint.
- Unfolding the definition (its let-binding is definitional): coareaJacobian M f x = Real.sqrt(det(L ∘ L*)).

Facts about normDet used below (Mathlib Analysis/InnerProductSpace/NormDet.lean):
- normDet ≥ 0.
- For X between spaces of equal finite dimension, normDet(X) = |det| of the matrix of X in any orthonormal bases (normDet_eq_norm_det_toMatrix).
- normDet(X.codRestrict p) = normDet(X) (normDet_codRestrict). So following a map by the isometric inclusion of a subspace does not change normDet.

Part (1).
1. LL* is self-adjoint and positive semidefinite, since ⟨LL*v, v⟩ = |L*v|² ≥ 0 for v ∈ ℝᵐ. Hence det(LL*) ≥ 0 (a product of nonnegative eigenvalues), and Real.sqrt(det(LL*)) = 0 iff det(LL*) = 0.
2. ker(LL*) = ker(L*): if LL*v = 0 then |L*v|² = ⟨LL*v, v⟩ = 0. Also ker(L*) = (range L)^⊥. Hence the following are equivalent: det(LL*) = 0; LL* is not injective; (range L)^⊥ ≠ 0; range L ≠ ℝᵐ; L is not surjective. (Equivalently, apply SimonGMT coareaLinearJacobian_eq_sqrt_det and coareaLinearJacobian_eq_zero_iff to the linear map L, after identifying (L ∘L adjoint L).det with (L ∘ₗ L.adjoint).det.) With step 1: coareaJacobian M f x = 0 iff L is not surjective.
3. Since T = range A, range L = D(T) = D(range A) = range(D ∘ A). So L is surjective iff D ∘ A = (fderiv ℝ f x).comp A is surjective. Steps 2 and 3 prove (1).

Part (2). Let P := WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ) and p₁ := WithLp.fst p. Define i₁ : ℝᵐ → P, a ↦ toLp(a,0), and j : ℝᵏ → P, b ↦ toLp(0,b). These are linear isometries onto the orthogonal subspaces P₁ = {toLp(a,0)} and P₂ = {toLp(0,b)}, and P = P₁ ⊕ P₂ (the inner product of P is the sum of the component inner products).
4. A is injective with range T. So Ã : P → T, Ã p := A p, is a linear isomorphism, dim T = m + k, and A = ι ∘ Ã. Hence normDet(A) = normDet(Ã) = |det Ã| in orthonormal bases. The hypothesis D(A p) = p₁ says L ∘ Ã = fst, where fst(p) := p₁; in particular L is surjective. Let Q := ker L ⊆ T and let Q^⊥ be its orthogonal complement in T. By rank–nullity, dim Q = k and dim Q^⊥ = m.
5. For b ∈ ℝᵏ, L(Ã(j b)) = fst(toLp(0,b)) = 0, so Ã(j b) ∈ Q. Thus Θ₂ := Ã ∘ j : ℝᵏ → Q is an injective linear map between k-dimensional spaces, hence an isomorphism. Since B b = A(toLp(0,b)) = ι(Θ₂ b), B is Θ₂ followed by the isometric inclusion Q → ℝᴺ. Therefore normDet(B) = normDet(Θ₂) = |det Θ₂|, using orthonormal bases of ℝᵏ and Q.
6. Let π₁ : T → Q^⊥ and π₂ : T → Q be the orthogonal projections, and set α := π₁ ∘ Ã ∘ i₁ : ℝᵐ → Q^⊥ and β := π₂ ∘ Ã ∘ i₁ : ℝᵐ → Q. Use two orthonormal bases:
   - on P: i₁ of the standard basis of ℝᵐ followed by j of the standard basis of ℝᵏ;
   - on T: an orthonormal basis of Q^⊥ followed by one of Q.
   The column of Ã at i₁(e_i) has Q^⊥-coordinates α e_i and Q-coordinates β e_i. The column at j(e_l) is Θ₂ e_l ∈ Q (step 5). So the matrix of Ã is the block matrix [[α, 0], [β, Θ₂]], which is block lower triangular. Hence |det Ã| = |det α|·|det Θ₂|.
7. Since L vanishes on Q, L t = L(π₁ t) for every t ∈ T. Let λ := L|_{Q^⊥} : Q^⊥ → ℝᵐ. For a ∈ ℝᵐ, λ(α a) = L(π₁ Ã(i₁ a)) = L(Ã(i₁ a)) = fst(toLp(a,0)) = a, i.e. λ ∘ α = id on ℝᵐ. Both maps are between m-dimensional spaces, so in orthonormal bases det(λ)·det(α) = 1, hence |det λ|·|det α| = 1.
8. L = λ ∘ π₁, so L* = π₁* ∘ λ*, where π₁* : Q^⊥ → T is the inclusion and π₁ ∘ π₁* = id on Q^⊥. Hence LL* = λλ*. If Λ is the matrix of λ in an orthonormal basis of Q^⊥ and the standard basis of ℝᵐ, then LL* has matrix ΛΛᵀ. So det(LL*) = (det Λ)² and coareaJacobian M f x = √det(LL*) = |det λ|. (This is also SimonGMT coareaHorizontalLinear_normDet with coareaLinearJacobian_eq_sqrt_det: normDet(L|_{(ker L)^⊥}) = √det(L L*).)
9. Combining steps 4–8: coareaJacobian M f x · normDet(A) = |det λ|·|det α|·|det Θ₂| = |det Θ₂| = normDet(B). The degenerate cases are covered:
   - if m = 0, then LL* is the identity of the zero space, coareaJacobian M f x = 1, and α, λ are maps of zero-dimensional spaces with determinant 1;
   - if k = 0, then Q = 0, Θ₂ is the map of zero-dimensional spaces, and normDet(B) = 1.
proof_key_steps: LL* is positive semidefinite and ker(LL*) = ker L* = (range L)^⊥, so √det(LL*) = 0 iff L is not surjective.
range L = D(range A) = range(D∘A), which gives part (1).
For (2): Ã : P → T is an isomorphism with L∘Ã = fst; Q = ker L has dimension k and Θ₂ = Ã∘j : ℝᵏ → Q is an isomorphism, so normDet(B) = |det Θ₂| and normDet(A) = |det Ã|.
In orthonormal bases adapted to P₁⊕P₂ and Q^⊥⊕Q the matrix of Ã is block lower triangular [[α,0],[β,Θ₂]], so |det Ã| = |det α|·|det Θ₂|.
λ := L|_{Q^⊥} satisfies λ∘α = id and LL* = λλ*, so √det(LL*) = |det λ| = 1/|det α|; multiply.

subproblems.title: Critical fibres of a C¹ map ℝ^{m+k} → ℝᵐ are Hᵏ-null for almost every value
subproblems.statement: Let m, k ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^{m+k} open, and G : ℝ^{m+k} → ℝᵐ of class C¹ on V. Then for Lᵐ-almost every y ∈ ℝᵐ, μHE[k]({x ∈ V : DG(x) is not surjective} ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0. Here μHE[k] is Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^{m+k} and Lᵐ = volume.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m k : ℕ) (V : Set (Rn (m + k))) (G : Rn (m + k) → Rn m), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 G V → ∀ᵐ y ∂(volume : Measure (Rn m)), μHE[k] ({x | x ∈ V ∧ ¬ Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ G x)} ∩ G ⁻¹' {y}) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1.1 of the parent proof, extended from a compact Q ⊆ V to all of V by a countable exhaustion.

Notation.
- n := m + k and C_G := {x ∈ V : fderiv ℝ G x is not surjective}.
- Lⁿ and Lᵐ are Lebesgue measures (volume).
- μH[k] is Mathlib's k-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝⁿ, and μHE[k] = c_k·μH[k] with the finite constant c_k := addHaarScalarFactor(volume, μH[k]) (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def).
Since G is C¹ on the open set V, G is differentiable at each x ∈ V and x ↦ DG(x) is continuous on V.

1. If m = 0, every linear map into ℝ⁰ is surjective, so C_G = ∅ and the claim is trivial. Assume m ≥ 1 from now on.
2. Reduction to compact pieces. The open set V is the union of the countably many closed balls with rational centre and positive rational radius that are contained in V; these are compact sets Q_j ⊆ V. It suffices to show: for every compact Q ⊆ V there is an Lᵐ-null set Z_Q with μH[k](Q ∩ C_G ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0 for all y ∉ Z_Q. Then, for y outside the null set ∪_j Z_{Q_j},
   μHE[k](C_G ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = c_k·μH[k](C_G ∩ G⁻¹{y}) ≤ c_k·Σ_j μH[k](Q_j ∩ C_G ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0.
   Fix a compact Q ⊆ V and let K′ := Q ∩ C_G. If K′ = ∅, take Z_Q = ∅; so assume K′ ≠ ∅.
3. Constants.
   - Choose ρ₀ > 0 with K₁ := {z : dist(z,Q) ≤ ρ₀} ⊆ V (possible since Q is compact and V open). K₁ is closed and bounded, hence compact, and Lⁿ(K₁) < ∞.
   - Let L_G := sup_{z∈K₁} ‖DG(z)‖ < ∞.
   - For 0 < r ≤ ρ₀ let ω(r) := sup{‖DG(z) − DG(x)‖ : x ∈ Q, |z − x| ≤ r}. All such z lie in K₁, and DG is uniformly continuous on the compact K₁, so ω(r) → 0 as r → 0⁺.
   - Let ω_n := Lⁿ(B(0,1)) ∈ (0,∞), so that Lⁿ(B(z,s)) = ω_n sⁿ.
4. Images of balls centred at critical points. Let x ∈ K′ and 0 < r ≤ ρ₀. The closed ball B̄(x,r) is convex and contained in K₁ ⊆ V.
   The map z ↦ G(z) − DG(x)z is differentiable on B̄(x,r), with derivative DG(z) − DG(x) of norm ≤ ω(r). By the mean value inequality, |G(z) − G(x) − DG(x)(z − x)| ≤ ω(r)|z − x| ≤ ω(r) r for z ∈ B̄(x,r).
   Since DG(x) is not surjective and m ≥ 1, there is a unit vector e₁ ⊥ range DG(x); complete it to an orthonormal basis e₁, …, e_m of ℝᵐ. For z ∈ B̄(x,r) put v := G(z) − G(x). Then
   - |⟨v,e₁⟩| = |⟨v − DG(x)(z − x), e₁⟩| ≤ ω(r) r;
   - for i ≥ 2, |⟨v,e_i⟩| ≤ |v| ≤ ‖DG(x)‖ r + ω(r) r ≤ (L_G + ω(r)) r, using x ∈ K₁.
   Hence G(B̄(x,r)) ⊆ G(x) + Θ(R_r), where Θ is the linear isometry of ℝᵐ sending the standard basis to (e_i) and R_r := [−ω(r)r, ω(r)r] × [−(L_G+ω(r))r, (L_G+ω(r))r]^{m−1}. Translations and linear isometries preserve Lᵐ, so
   Lᵐ(G(B̄(x,r))) ≤ Lᵐ(R_r) = 2ᵐ ω(r)(L_G + ω(r))^{m−1} rᵐ.
   Moreover G(B̄(x,r)) is compact (a continuous image of a compact subset of V), hence Borel.
5. Packing. Fix 0 < r ≤ ρ₀. Suppose x₁, …, x_p ∈ K′ satisfy |x_i − x_j| ≥ r for i ≠ j. Then the open balls B(x_i, r/2) are pairwise disjoint and contained in K₁ (dist(z,Q) ≤ |z − x_i| < r/2 ≤ ρ₀). So p·ω_n(r/2)ⁿ ≤ Lⁿ(K₁), i.e. p ≤ P(r) := 2ⁿ Lⁿ(K₁)/(ω_n rⁿ).
   Since K′ ≠ ∅ and these cardinalities are bounded, choose such an r-separated family x₁, …, x_p of maximal cardinality. It cannot be enlarged, so every x ∈ K′ has |x − x_i| < r for some i. Hence K′ ⊆ ∪_{i≤p} B̄(x_i, r).
6. Covering estimate. For δ > 0 and S ⊆ ℝⁿ let h_δ(S) be the infimum of Σ_l [t_l ≠ ∅]·(diam t_l)^k over all sequences (t_l) of sets with S ⊆ ∪_l t_l and diam t_l ≤ δ. By Mathlib's hausdorffMeasure_apply, μH[k](S) = sup_{δ>0} h_δ(S), and h_δ(S) increases as δ decreases.
   Let y ∈ ℝᵐ and 2r ≤ δ. Put t_i := B̄(x_i,r) ∩ K′ ∩ G⁻¹{y} for i ≤ p, and t_l := ∅ for l > p. These sets cover K′ ∩ G⁻¹{y} (step 5) and have diameter ≤ 2r ≤ δ; moreover t_i ≠ ∅ only if y ∈ G(B̄(x_i,r)). Therefore
   h_δ(K′ ∩ G⁻¹{y}) ≤ S_r(y) := Σ_{i=1}^p (2r)^k·1_{G(B̄(x_i,r))}(y).
   S_r is Borel. By steps 4–5, and using rᵏ·rᵐ = rⁿ (since n = m + k),
   ∫ S_r dLᵐ = Σ_{i≤p} (2r)^k Lᵐ(G(B̄(x_i,r))) ≤ P(r)(2r)^k 2ᵐ ω(r)(L_G+ω(r))^{m−1} rᵐ = ε(r),
   where ε(r) := 2^{n+k+m} Lⁿ(K₁) ω(r)(L_G+ω(r))^{m−1}/ω_n. By step 3, ε(r) → 0 as r → 0⁺.
7. Fatou. Take r_j ∈ (0,ρ₀] with r_j → 0 and let S_j := S_{r_j}, built from a family as in step 5 for r = r_j. By Fatou's lemma (lintegral_liminf_le),
   ∫ liminf_j S_j dLᵐ ≤ liminf_j ∫ S_j dLᵐ ≤ liminf_j ε(r_j) = 0.
   So Z_Q := {y : liminf_j S_j(y) ≠ 0} is a Borel Lᵐ-null set. Let y ∉ Z_Q and δ > 0. For all large j, 2r_j ≤ δ, and then h_δ(K′ ∩ G⁻¹{y}) ≤ S_j(y) by step 6. Hence h_δ(K′ ∩ G⁻¹{y}) ≤ liminf_j S_j(y) = 0. Taking the supremum over δ > 0 gives μH[k](Q ∩ C_G ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = μH[k](K′ ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0 for all y ∉ Z_Q.
8. Steps 2 and 7 prove that μHE[k]({x ∈ V : DG(x) not surjective} ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0 for Lᵐ-almost every y.
proof_key_steps: m = 0 is trivial; reduce to K′ = Q ∩ C_G for compact Q ⊆ V via a countable cover of V by compact balls.
Mean value inequality and a unit normal e₁ ⊥ range DG(x): G(B̄(x,r)) lies in a rotated box of Lᵐ-measure ≤ 2ᵐ ω(r)(L_G+ω(r))^{m−1} rᵐ.
A maximal r-separated family in K′ has at most 2ⁿLⁿ(K₁)/(ω_n rⁿ) points, and its closed r-balls cover K′.
h_δ(K′∩G⁻¹y) ≤ S_r(y) := Σ(2r)^k 1_{G(B̄(x_i,r))}(y) for 2r ≤ δ, with ∫S_r ≤ 2^{n+k+m}Lⁿ(K₁)ω(r)(L_G+ω(r))^{m−1}/ω_n → 0, using n = m+k.
Fatou along r_j → 0 gives h_δ(K′∩G⁻¹y) = 0 for every δ and a.e. y, so μH[k] = 0 and μHE[k] = c_k·μH[k] = 0; take a countable union over the compact pieces.

Then for Lᵐ-almost every y ∈ ℝᵐ, μHE[k](M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ {x : coareaJacobian M f x = 0}) = 0.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1.2 of the parent proof.

Notation: n := m + k and C := {x : coareaJacobian M f x = 0}. Since U is open and f is C¹ on U, f is differentiable at every point of U.

1. Countable atlas. For each z ∈ M, the submanifold hypothesis gives V_z ⊆ ℝⁿ, W_z ⊆ ℝᴺ and ψ_z with z ∈ W_z and IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 M V_z W_z ψ_z. In particular V_z and W_z are open, ψ_z is C¹ on V_z, and ψ_z(V_z) = W_z ∩ M. The open sets W_z cover M, and ℝᴺ is second countable. So (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable) there is a countable set I ⊆ M with ∪_{z∈I} W_z = ∪_{z∈M} W_z ⊇ M.
2. One chart. Fix z ∈ M and write V, W, ψ for V_z, W_z, ψ_z. For x ∈ V, ψ(x) ∈ W ∩ M ⊆ U. Let G := f ∘ ψ. G is C¹ on V as a composition, since ψ maps V into U. For x ∈ V the chain rule gives DG(x) = Df(ψ x) ∘ Dψ(x): ψ is differentiable at x because V is open, and f is differentiable at ψ(x) ∈ U.
3. Critical points. Let x ∈ V with coareaJacobian M f (ψ x) = 0. By hT, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = range Dψ(x). By child coarea_jacobian_linear_algebra, part (1), with A := Dψ(x), the map Df(ψ x) ∘ Dψ(x) = DG(x) is not surjective. So x ∈ C_G := {x ∈ V : DG(x) not surjective}. Consequently, for every y,
   (W ∩ M) ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ C ⊆ ψ(C_G ∩ G⁻¹{y}).
   Indeed, a point of W ∩ M = ψ(V) is ψ(x) with x ∈ V, and f(ψ x) = y means G(x) = y.
4. Lipschitz pieces. For each x ∈ V choose ε_x > 0 with B̄(x, ε_x) ⊆ V. The open balls B(x, ε_x) cover V, so by second countability countably many of them, indexed by a countable set I_V ⊆ V, cover V. Hence V ⊆ ∪_{x∈I_V} B̄(x, ε_x). Each B̄(x, ε_x) is convex and compact, and ψ is C¹ on it, so ψ is K_x-Lipschitz on B̄(x, ε_x) for some K_x (ContDiffOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith).
5. Null fibres in one chart. Apply child coarea_critical_fibers_null_euclidean to V and G: there is an Lᵐ-null set Z_z such that μHE[k](C_G ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0 for y ∉ Z_z. Fix such a y. For x ∈ I_V, the Lipschitz image bound for Hausdorff measure (SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn) gives
   μHE[k](ψ(B̄(x,ε_x) ∩ C_G ∩ G⁻¹{y})) ≤ K_x^k·μHE[k](B̄(x,ε_x) ∩ C_G ∩ G⁻¹{y}) ≤ K_x^k·μHE[k](C_G ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0.
   Since C_G ⊆ V ⊆ ∪_{x∈I_V} B̄(x,ε_x), step 3 gives
   (W ∩ M) ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ C ⊆ ∪_{x∈I_V} ψ(B̄(x,ε_x) ∩ C_G ∩ G⁻¹{y}),
   a countable union of μHE[k]-null sets. Hence μHE[k](W_z ∩ M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ C) = 0 for y ∉ Z_z.
6. Conclusion. Z := ∪_{z∈I} Z_z is Lᵐ-null as a countable union. For y ∉ Z, step 1 gives M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ C ⊆ ∪_{z∈I} (W_z ∩ M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ C), so μHE[k](M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ C) ≤ Σ_{z∈I} 0 = 0.
proof_key_steps: Countably many Simon charts (V_z, W_z, ψ_z) with M ⊆ ∪W_z, by second countability.
On a chart, G := f∘ψ is C¹ on V with DG(x) = Df(ψx)∘Dψ(x); hT and child (1) turn coareaJacobian M f (ψx) = 0 into x ∈ C_G, so (W∩M)∩f⁻¹y∩C ⊆ ψ(C_G∩G⁻¹y).
Child coarea_critical_fibers_null_euclidean: μHE[k](C_G∩G⁻¹y) = 0 off an Lᵐ-null set.
ψ is Lipschitz on countably many closed balls covering V, and Lipschitz images of μHE[k]-null sets are null.
Take a countable union over the charts.

Source: Step 2 of the parent proof. Relative properness of the new chart is not needed and is not asserted. The tangent identity is derived directly from the original chart.

Notation: n := m + k and P := WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ), an inner product space of dimension n; for p ∈ P, p₁ := WithLp.fst p. Since U is open and f is C¹ on U, f is differentiable at every point of U.

1. A chart at x₀. The submanifold hypothesis gives open V ⊆ ℝⁿ, open W ⊆ ℝᴺ and ψ with x₀ ∈ W and IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 M V W ψ. That is: ψ is C¹ on V, injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, and Dψ(x) is injective for x ∈ V. Since x₀ ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), x₀ = ψ(x₀′) for some x₀′ ∈ V. Put G := f ∘ ψ. As ψ(V) ⊆ M ⊆ U, G is C¹ on V and DG(x) = Df(ψ x) ∘ Dψ(x) for x ∈ V (chain rule).
2. DG(x₀′) is surjective. By hT, tangentSpace M x₀ = range Dψ(x₀′). By child coarea_jacobian_linear_algebra part (1), with A := Dψ(x₀′), the hypothesis coareaJacobian M f x₀ ≠ 0 implies that Df(x₀) ∘ Dψ(x₀′) = DG(x₀′) is surjective. By rank–nullity, K₀ := ker DG(x₀′) ⊆ ℝⁿ has dimension n − m = k.
3. Completing G to a local diffeomorphism. Since dim K₀ = k = dim ℝᵏ, there is a linear isomorphism e : K₀ → ℝᵏ. Let π := e ∘ P_{K₀} : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ, where P_{K₀} is the orthogonal projection onto K₀; π is linear and π|_{K₀} = e is injective. Define Φ : ℝⁿ → P by Φ(x) := toLp(G(x), π(x − x₀′)). Then Φ is C¹ on V with DΦ(x)v = toLp(DG(x)v, πv).
4. DΦ(x₀′) is invertible. If DG(x₀′)v = 0 and πv = 0, then v ∈ K₀ and e(v) = πv = 0, so v = 0. Thus DΦ(x₀′) : ℝⁿ → P is an injective linear map between spaces of the same dimension n, hence a linear isomorphism.
5. Inverse function theorem.
   - The set V′ := {x ∈ V : DΦ(x) is invertible} is open (DΦ is continuous on V and invertible operators form an open set) and contains x₀′.
   - Apply the C¹ inverse function theorem at x₀′ (Mathlib ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph) and intersect its source with V′. This gives an open V₁ with x₀′ ∈ V₁ ⊆ V′ ⊆ V such that Ω := Φ(V₁) is open in P and Φ|_{V₁} : V₁ → Ω is a homeomorphism. Let Λ : Ω → V₁ be its inverse.
   - For every x ∈ V₁, Φ is C¹ near x with invertible derivative. So Λ is C¹ at every p ∈ Ω with DΛ(p) = DΦ(Λ p)⁻¹ (OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm). In particular DΛ(p) is a linear isomorphism P → ℝⁿ.
   (Mathlib's implicit function theorem, HasStrictFDerivAt.implicitToOpenPartialHomeomorph in Analysis/Calculus/Implicit.lean, yields the same chart up to the linear identification ker DG(x₀′) ≅ ℝᵏ and ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ ≅ P.)
6. Define Ψ := ψ ∘ Λ, using the global extension of Λ given by the partial homeomorphism; values off Ω are irrelevant. Then:
   (a) Ψ is C¹ on Ω: Λ is C¹ on Ω with Λ(Ω) = V₁ ⊆ V, and ψ is C¹ on V.
   (b) Ψ is injective on Ω: Λ is injective on Ω and ψ is injective on V.
   (c) For p ∈ Ω, DΨ(p) = Dψ(Λ p) ∘ DΛ(p) by the chain rule, and this is a composition of injective linear maps.
   (d) Apply SimonGMT IsSimonLocalRepresentation.exists_open_image_eq_inter (Simon 4.2) to the open set V₁ ⊆ V: there is an open O ⊆ W with ψ(V₁) = O ∩ M. Then Ψ(Ω) = ψ(Λ(Ω)) = ψ(V₁) = O ∩ M, and x₀ = ψ(x₀′) ∈ ψ(V₁) ⊆ O.
   (e) For p ∈ Ω, Φ(Λ p) = p, and the first component of Φ(x) is G(x). Hence p₁ = G(Λ p) = f(ψ(Λ p)) = f(Ψ p).
   (f) For p ∈ Ω we have Λ p ∈ V. So by hT, tangentSpace M (Ψ p) = tangentSpace M (ψ(Λ p)) = range Dψ(Λ p). Since DΛ(p) is surjective, range Dψ(Λ p) = range(Dψ(Λ p) ∘ DΛ(p)) = range DΨ(p).
Thus Ω, O and Ψ have all the required properties.
proof_key_steps: Pick a Simon chart ψ with x₀ = ψ(x₀′); G := f∘ψ is C¹ with DG = Df∘Dψ.
hT and child part (1): coareaJacobian M f x₀ ≠ 0 implies DG(x₀′) is surjective, so K₀ = ker DG(x₀′) has dimension k.
Φ(x) := (G(x), π(x − x₀′)), with π injective on K₀, has invertible derivative at x₀′; the C¹ inverse function theorem gives Φ : V₁ → Ω with C¹ inverse Λ and DΛ invertible on Ω.
Ψ := ψ∘Λ is C¹ and injective with injective derivative; Ψ(Ω) = ψ(V₁) = O ∩ M by Simon 4.2, and f∘Ψ = first component.
range DΨ(p) = range Dψ(Λp) = tangentSpace M (Ψp) by hT, because DΛ(p) is invertible.

subproblems.statement: Let N, m, k ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝᴺ, f : ℝᴺ → ℝᵐ and P := WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ). Let Ω ⊆ P be open and Ψ : P → ℝᴺ be C¹ on Ω and injective on Ω, with DΨ(p) injective for p ∈ Ω. Assume that for every p ∈ Ω: f is differentiable at Ψ(p), f(Ψ p) = WithLp.fst p, and tangentSpace M (Ψ p) = range DΨ(p). Let S ⊆ Ψ(Ω) be a Borel set and g : ℝᴺ → [0,∞] Borel measurable. Then y ↦ ∫_{S∩f⁻¹{y}} g dμHE[k] is Borel measurable on ℝᵐ, and ∫_S g·coareaJacobian M f dμHE[m+k] = ∫_{ℝᵐ} ∫_{S∩f⁻¹{y}} g dμHE[k] dLᵐ(y).

Source: Step 3 of the parent proof.

Notation and standard facts.
- P := WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ) is an inner product space with finrank_ℝ P = m + k.
- toLp(a,b) ∈ P for a ∈ ℝᵐ, b ∈ ℝᵏ; p₁ := WithLp.fst p and p₂ := WithLp.snd p.
- (a,b) ↦ toLp(a,b) is measure preserving from volume on ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ (= Lᵐ ⊗ Lᵏ) to volume on P (WithLp.volume_preserving_toLp).
- On every finite-dimensional inner product space E, μHE[finrank E] = volume (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), and finrank ℝᵏ = k.
- j : ℝᵏ → P, j(b) := toLp(0,b), is a linear isometry.
- For a ∈ ℝᵐ, the fibre map is Ψ_a(b) := Ψ(toLp(a,b)) and its domain is Ω_a := {b : toLp(a,b) ∈ Ω}, which is open.
- For p ∈ Ω put J(p) := normDet(DΨ(p)) = areaJacobianAt Ψ p and J_v(p) := normDet(DΨ(p) ∘ j).
- J*f := coareaJacobian M f ≥ 0, since it is a real square root.

1. Derivatives.
   - For p ∈ Ω, Ψ is differentiable at p (C¹ on the open set Ω).
   - For b ∈ Ω_a, the map b ↦ toLp(a,b) = toLp(a,0) + j(b) is affine with derivative j. So Ψ_a is differentiable at b with DΨ_a(b) = DΨ(toLp(a,b)) ∘ j. This map is injective because j and DΨ are injective, and Ψ_a is injective on Ω_a.
   - f ∘ Ψ coincides on the open set Ω with the continuous linear map p ↦ p₁, so D(f ∘ Ψ)(p) = (q ↦ q₁). Since f is differentiable at Ψ(p), the chain rule gives Df(Ψ p)(DΨ(p) q) = q₁ for all q ∈ P.
2. Pointwise Jacobian identity. Let p = toLp(a,b) ∈ Ω. Apply child coarea_jacobian_linear_algebra part (2) with:
   - x := Ψ(p);
   - A := DΨ(p), which is injective, has range tangentSpace M (Ψ p) by hypothesis, and satisfies Df(x)(A q) = q₁ by step 1;
   - B := DΨ_a(b), which satisfies B b′ = A(toLp(0,b′)) by step 1.
   It gives J*f(Ψ p)·J(p) = normDet(DΨ_a(b)) = J_v(p).
3. Pull-back of the left side. S′ := Ω ∩ Ψ⁻¹(S) is a Borel subset of P (Ψ is continuous on the open set Ω, and S is Borel). Since S ⊆ Ψ(Ω), Ψ(S′) = S. Apply SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_volume_of_injective_derivative with E := P, s := S′, the map Ψ (differentiable with injective derivative on S′ and injective on S′) and the weight w(x) := g(x)·ofReal(J*f(x)). Since finrank P = m + k,
   ∫_S g·ofReal(J*f) dμHE[m+k] = ∫_{S′} ofReal(J(p))·g(Ψ p)·ofReal(J*f(Ψ p)) dp = ∫_P H(p) dp,
   where H(p) := 1_{S′}(p)·g(Ψ p)·ofReal(J_v(p)). The last equality uses step 2 and ofReal(J*f(Ψp))·ofReal(J(p)) = ofReal(J*f(Ψp)·J(p)), valid because both factors are ≥ 0.
4. H is Borel.
   - p ↦ DΨ(p) is Borel (measurable_fderiv); composing with j is continuous, and normDet is continuous (SimonGMT continuous_normDet). So J_v is Borel.
   - Ψ is continuous on the open (hence Borel) set Ω, so p ↦ 1_Ω(p)·g(Ψ p) is Borel.
   - S′ ⊆ Ω is Borel.
   Hence H is Borel.
5. Tonelli. Using the measure-preserving map toLp and Tonelli on ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ (lintegral_prod), ∫_P H dp = ∫_{ℝᵐ} F(a) da, where F(a) := ∫_{ℝᵏ} H(toLp(a,b)) db. F is Borel by Measurable.lintegral_prod_right', applied to the Borel function (a,b) ↦ H(toLp(a,b)).
6. Fibrewise area formula. Fix a ∈ ℝᵐ and let S′_a := {b : toLp(a,b) ∈ S′}, a Borel subset of Ω_a.
   Claim: Ψ_a(S′_a) = S ∩ f⁻¹{a}.
   - If b ∈ S′_a, then Ψ_a(b) = Ψ(toLp(a,b)) ∈ S and f(Ψ_a(b)) = (toLp(a,b))₁ = a.
   - Conversely, let x ∈ S with f(x) = a. Then x = Ψ(p) for some p ∈ Ω (because S ⊆ Ψ(Ω)), so p ∈ S′. Also a = f(Ψ p) = p₁, so p = toLp(a, p₂), p₂ ∈ S′_a and Ψ_a(p₂) = x.
   Now apply SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_volume_of_injective_derivative with E := ℝᵏ, s := S′_a, the map Ψ_a (differentiable with injective derivative on S′_a ⊆ Ω_a and injective there, by step 1) and the weight g:
   ∫_{S∩f⁻¹{a}} g dμHE[k] = ∫_{S′_a} ofReal(normDet DΨ_a(b))·g(Ψ_a b) db = ∫_{ℝᵏ} H(toLp(a,b)) db = F(a).
   The middle equality holds because normDet DΨ_a(b) = J_v(toLp(a,b)) for b ∈ S′_a (step 1), and H(toLp(a,b)) = 0 for b ∉ S′_a.
7. Conclusion. By step 6, y ↦ ∫_{S∩f⁻¹{y}} g dμHE[k] equals F at every point, so it is Borel by step 5. By steps 3, 5 and 6,
   ∫_S g·J*f dμHE[m+k] = ∫_P H = ∫_{ℝᵐ} F(a) da = ∫_{ℝᵐ} ∫_{S∩f⁻¹{a}} g dμHE[k] da.
proof_key_steps: Chain rule on the open set Ω: Df(Ψp)∘DΨ(p) is the first-component map, and the fibre map Ψ_a(b) = Ψ(toLp(a,b)) has DΨ_a(b) = DΨ(toLp(a,b))∘j.
Child part (2) gives J*f(Ψp)·normDet DΨ(p) = normDet DΨ_a(b) pointwise on Ω.
The weighted area formula for Ψ on S′ = Ω∩Ψ⁻¹S turns ∫_S g·J*f dμHE[m+k] into ∫_P 1_{S′}·g(Ψ)·normDet(DΨ∘j).
Tonelli through WithLp.volume_preserving_toLp writes this as ∫_a ∫_b, with the inner integral Borel in a.
The fibrewise area formula for Ψ_a on S′_a, with Ψ_a(S′_a) = S∩f⁻¹{a}, identifies the inner integral with ∫_{S∩f⁻¹{a}} g dμHE[k] for every a.

Source: Step 4 of the parent proof.

Notation: J*f := coareaJacobian M f, μ := μHE[m+k], ν := μHE[k] and P := WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ).

1. Preliminaries.
   - f is differentiable at each point of U, since it is C¹ on the open set U.
   - For y ∈ ℝᵐ, U ∩ f⁻¹{y} = U ∖ (U ∩ f⁻¹(ℝᵐ∖{y})), and U ∩ f⁻¹(ℝᵐ∖{y}) is open because f is continuous on the open set U. So U ∩ f⁻¹{y} is Borel.
   - Consequently X ∩ f⁻¹{y} = X ∩ (U ∩ f⁻¹{y}) is Borel for every Borel X ⊆ U.
2. Charts covering the regular set. Let R := {x ∈ M : J*f(x) ≠ 0}.
   - For each x ∈ R, child coarea_exists_straightening_chart gives (Ω_x, O_x, Ψ_x): Ω_x ⊆ P open; O_x open with x ∈ O_x; Ψ_x C¹ and injective on Ω_x with injective derivative; Ψ_x(Ω_x) = O_x ∩ M; and f(Ψ_x p) = p₁ and tangentSpace M (Ψ_x p) = range DΨ_x(p) for p ∈ Ω_x.
   - ℝᴺ is second countable, so there is a countable T ⊆ R with ∪_{x∈T} O_x = ∪_{x∈R} O_x.
   - Choose a surjection e : ℕ → T ⊔ {∗}, for instance onto Option T, which is countable and nonempty. Set (Ω_n, O_n, Ψ_n) := (Ω_x, O_x, Ψ_x) if e(n) = x ∈ T, and (∅, ∅, 0) if e(n) = ∗.
   - Every (Ω_n, O_n, Ψ_n) has all the chart properties above. For the empty chart they hold vacuously, and Ψ_n(∅) = ∅ = ∅ ∩ M. So Ψ_n(Ω_n) = O_n ∩ M for all n.
